text:
A stonecutter spent his days chipping rocks from a mountain. It was heavy, boring work, and he often complained. “If only I were rich,” he muttered, “life would be so much easier.”

One day, a mountain spirit heard him. “Your wish is granted,” it said. In an instant, the stonecutter became a wealthy merchant, living in a splendid house.

He was delighted, until he saw a prince riding by with a hundred servants. “The prince has far more power than I do,” he thought. “If only I were a prince!” At once, he became one.

But as a prince, he suffered from the heat of the sun. “The sun is stronger than any king,” he said. “I wish I were the sun.” And so he became the sun, burning brightly in the sky.

Soon a cloud drifted across and blocked his light. “The cloud is mightier than I am!” he cried, and became a cloud. But the wind pushed him around the sky. So he became the wind, which was stopped only by a giant mountain that never moved.

“The mountain is the strongest of all,” he said. “I wish I were a mountain!”

At last, he was a mountain, enormous and unmovable. But he felt a sharp pain in his side. A small man with a hammer was chipping away at his stone. It was a stonecutter.

For the first time, the former stonecutter understood.

Moral: Envy blinds us to our own value, and happiness starts with appreciating who we are.

quiz.q: The stonecutter first became a rich merchant.
The stonecutter was happy as the sun.
Who was chipping away at the mountain?
___ blinds us to our own value.
